authorship: Cases and expected results written by hand by Claude (architect), checked against a separate Claude-only reference implementation, committed by Avi. Codex must never edit this file. If a case fails and you believe the expected value is wrong, stop and report the case ID and your reasoning.

interface.errors: WordsError is words.cards.WordsError, imported, never redefined.
interface.check_headline(text, claim_ids, page, re: Section 15.1. Returns a list of problems, each a string "<rule>: <detail>" with a non-empty detail. Never raises for a bad text or claim_ids.
interface.check_approvals(approvals, pages, regist: Section 15.2. Returns {asset id: headline} in the instrument list's order, or raises WordsError.

case_fields.page / pages: Page fixtures below (deep copies). They carry only the fields section 15 reads, plus a few for realism.
case_fields.text / claims: check_headline cases: passed as given (deep copies).
case_fields.expected_rules: check_headline cases: the rule names of the returned problems, each counted once, in the order they first appear (the part before ": "). Every problem must be a string with a rule name, ": " and a non-empty detail. [] means the headline passes.
case_fields.word_lists / list / template: word_list cases: for every entry of word_lists[list], in order, the text is template with {word} replaced by that entry, checked with check_headline against the named page and the given claims; each must give exactly expected_rules (as above). The lists are section 15.1's, word for word.
case_fields.approvals / approvals_edits: check_approvals cases: the named approvals fixture (deep copy) with approvals_edits applied with apply_edits.
case_fields.expected: check_approvals cases: the returned dictionary, compared with assert_result_equal (tolerance 0), and its keys in exactly this order.
case_fields.expected_error / message_must_contain: As in the other golden files.
